title: Kola Superdeep Borehole: the deepest hole ever dug

facts.claim: Soviet scientists began drilling the Kola Superdeep Borehole in 1970 on the Kola Peninsula in the Arctic north-west of Russia
By 1989 it reached 12,262 m, the deepest artificial hole ever drilled
The hole is only about 23 cm wide
Temperatures at the bottom reached about 180°C, far hotter than expected, and drilling stopped in 1992
Scientists found water deep in the rock and microscopic fossils of ancient plankton about 6 km down
The borehole is sealed with a welded metal cap

opening.label: KOLA PENINSULA · ARCTIC RUSSIA
opening.why: A remote Arctic spot almost nobody could place; 'where' adds to the wonder.

music_mood: cold and deep: slow descending pulse, metallic ticks

headline: 12 KM DOWN,
THEN THEY STOPPED
cover.hook_voiceover_ml: സോവിയറ്റുകാർ ഭൂമിയിലേക്ക് 12 കിലോമീറ്റർ കുഴിച്ചു. പിന്നെ എന്തോ ഒന്ന് അവരെ നിർത്തിച്ചു.
cover.visual: A snowy Arctic plain at night with a drilling tower; beneath it a thin, impossibly deep shaft drops into glowing dark rock.
cover.build_cmd: Top 35%: night sky (#070a14) with 60 stars and a faint green aurora band (3 wavy translucent strokes, drifting). Snow ground line at y0.33. A lattice drilling tower (triangular frame of thin lines) at x0.5 from y0.14 to y0.33. Below ground: rock layers (8 horizontal bands, browns to near-black) down to the bottom of the frame; a thin vertical shaft (10px, accent colour) extends downward from the tower, growing from y0.33 to y0.9 over the first 60% of the scene with a glowing tip. Keep the bottom 25% quiet (dark rock) for the text.

scenes.voiceover_ml: 1970-ൽ സോവിയറ്റ് യൂണിയൻ ഭൂമിയുടെ പുറംതോട് തുളയ്ക്കാൻ തുടങ്ങി.
scenes.headline: THE SOVIET EXPERIMENT
scenes.visual: The drill rig at work: a rotating drill head grinds down through rock layers, chips flying.
scenes.build_cmd: Cross-section: rock bands as in the cover. A drill string (grey vertical bar 24px) descends from the top with a cone-shaped bit at the end; the bit 'rotates' (alternating stripe pattern cycling at 8 Hz) and descends from y0.3 to y0.62 over the scene. Rock chips (20 small polygons) fly up and settle on either side. A depth tick mark appears every time the bit passes a band boundary (short accent dashes on the left).

scenes.voiceover_ml: 1989-ൽ അവർ 12,262 മീറ്ററിൽ എത്തി. കുഴിയുടെ വീതി? വെറും 23 സെന്റീമീറ്റർ!
scenes.headline: 12,262 METRES DOWN
scenes.visual: A tall vertical depth scale; the shaft races down past milestone ticks while the depth counter climbs; a side inset shows the tiny width compared to a dinner plate.
scenes.build_cmd: A vertical ruler on the left (x0.22) from y0.24 to y0.7 with 12 ticks labelled by short accent marks (no text in canvas). A bright line travels down the ruler from top to bottom over 10-70% with ease-in-out, leaving a glowing trail. On the right (x0.68 y0.46) an inset circle (radius 150) shows two concentric circles: a large plate-sized ring and a tiny 23-cm hole as a small filled disc (ratio ~1:4), pulsing once at 60%. End with the whole ruler lit.

scenes.voiceover_ml: പക്ഷേ അടിയിൽ ചൂട് 180 ഡിഗ്രി! 1992-ൽ ഡ്രില്ലിംഗ് നിർത്തി.
scenes.headline: 180°C AT THE BOTTOM
scenes.visual: The shaft tip glows red; a thermometer bar on the side shoots past its expected mark; the drill bit sags and stops.
scenes.build_cmd: Dark rock cross-section near the bottom of the shaft. The shaft tip (x0.5 y0.5) glows with a radial red-orange gradient that grows from radius 40 to 220 over 0-50%. A thermometer bar on the right (x0.84, y0.3-0.62): fills upward with a gradient yellow to red from 10% to 70%, passing a dashed 'expected' line at 45% height; the top portion pulses red. At 70% the drill bit outline tilts 6° and its rotation stripes stop; a thin crack network (5 lines) spreads from the tip at 80%.

scenes.voiceover_ml: ആറ് കിലോമീറ്റർ താഴെ പാറയ്ക്കുള്ളിൽ വെള്ളം! പിന്നെ പുരാതന സൂക്ഷ്മജീവികളുടെ ഫോസിലുകൾ!
scenes.headline: LIFE 6 KM DOWN
scenes.visual: A microscope circle over a rock core sample reveals tiny droplets in the pores and delicate round fossil shapes.
scenes.build_cmd: A cylindrical rock core (vertical rounded rect 180x600 at x0.3 y0.46, grey with speckles) on the left; on the right a magnifier circle (radius 230 at x0.68 y0.46) showing a zoomed texture: 30 pore shapes with 12 glowing blue droplets fading in over 10-50%, then 8 tiny spiral/round fossil shapes (thin white outlines) fading in over 50-90%. Slowly rotate the fossils ±3°. Connect core and magnifier with a thin line and a small dashed sample box on the core.

scenes.voiceover_ml: ഇന്ന് ആ കുഴി ഇരുമ്പ് മൂടിയിട്ട് അടച്ചു. 12 കിലോമീറ്റർ കുഴിച്ചിട്ടും, നമ്മൾ ഭൂമിയുടെ തൊലി പോലും കടന്നിട്ടില്ല.
scenes.headline: WE BARELY SCRATCHED IT
scenes.visual: A rusty metal cap on a concrete slab in the snow; then the camera pulls far back to show the whole Earth's crust with the 12 km hole as a barely visible scratch.
scenes.build_cmd: 0-40%: snow scene with a round rusty cap (disc 220px, #6a4a3a with 8 bolt dots) on a concrete slab, with a short welded seam highlight. 40-100%: zoom out (scale the whole first scene down to 0.12 into the top-centre) while an Earth cross-section wedge appears: a large arc of crust (band 90px thick, brown) over a red-orange mantle gradient filling the lower frame; the borehole is a 1-2px accent line only 1/3 into the crust band, with a pulsing ring around it so it can be seen. Hold the final wide view for the last 20%.

instagram_caption:
The deepest hole humans ever dug is 12 km down, and only 23 cm wide. 🕳️

Soviet scientists drilled the Kola Superdeep Borehole from 1970, reaching 12,262 m by 1989. At the bottom it was about 180°C, far hotter than expected, so drilling stopped in 1992. On the way they found water inside rock and microscopic fossils 6 km down. The hole is now welded shut. 🔩

And 12 km isn't even a third of the way through Earth's crust. 🌍
